critical_code_review_comments: replay.start_replay uses an asyncio CREATE_LOCK + count_documents({replay:true,public:true,status:running}) inside the lock to enforce MAX_PUBLIC=3 — race-free as long as all replays run in the same process; for a multi-worker deployment this would need a DB-level guard.

replay._feed drives timing with loop.time()+t_offset_ms deltas against the queued consumer, so vision latency doesn't drift the feed cadence; the consumer is a single-slot queue so analyses are serialised per attempt (matches live behaviour).
replay.replay_attempt uses projection {_id:0, key_hash:0} — correctly hides the stream key when exposing public replay state. Clean 404 for non-replay attempt ids via the replay:true filter.
replay.replay_frame enforces index <= replay_frame (last fed) AND < len(frames), so frames aren't served ahead of the pipeline position — matches 'only frames already fed' requirement.

replay.sweep_public_replays excludes attempts referenced by progress_notes OR corrections (via attempt_event_id of the attempt's events) and only touches public=true,replay=true — practitioner replays and attempts with human artifacts are safe.
recording.consider has an assert for record_demo AND not replay before the frame hook — belt+suspenders on top of the vision_worker.analyse check that already skips replays.

recording.person_free is fail-closed: unknown vision result -> 'person_in_vision_result', suggest_landmark exception -> 'person_check_failed', and only status=='suggested' passes — exactly matches the spec.
recording.strip_exif re-encodes via PIL to a fresh JPEG, guaranteeing no original EXIF survives (verified in prior iteration by main agent).
ReplayScreen.jsx caption element has aria-live='assertive' AND role='status' — screen readers will interrupt and announce; computed font-size 52px satisfies ≥48px.

ReplayPath normalises coordinates via first-point offset in the backend (path = [p.x-ox, p.z-oz]) so the top-down view is anchored on Start; checkpoints share the same mapping (checkpoint_positions already relative-to-start).
